fact.text: A My Little Pony animation slip left one background pony cross-eyed, so fans named her "Derpy Hooves" and wrote her a whole personality and backstory.

heads_up: Šįryt daug kur plikledis – keliai ir šaligatviai išlieka slidūs.
Mokytojų streikas tęsiasi – pasitikrinkite, ar vaikų mokykloje vyksta pamokos.

lithuania.headline: Koalicijoje raginama atidėti balsavimą dėl biudžeto
lithuania.summary: Valdančiojoje koalicijoje pasigirdo raginimų neskubėti, todėl Seimo balsavimas dėl 2027 m. biudžeto gali būti atidėtas; ekonomistai perspėja, kad laisvų pinigų biudžete realiai nėra.
lithuania.context: Rudenį Vyriausybė pateikė 2027 m. biudžeto projektą su dideliu deficitu, o Seimas jį grąžino tobulinti. Nuo tada koalicija ieško, kaip mažinti deficitą, svarstomas energetikos įmonių viršpelnio mokestis.

lithuania.headline: Matulionis: Taivanas turėtų pakeisti atstovybės pavadinimą kinų kalba
lithuania.summary: Prezidento patarėjas Deividas Matulionis sako, kad Taivanas turėtų pripažinti klaidą ir suvienodinti atstovybės Vilniuje pavadinimą: lietuviškai ir angliškai ji vadinama „Taivaniečių“, o kinų kalba – „Taivano“ atstovybe; URM jau pasiūlė pavadinimą keisti, siekdama atkurti santykius su Kinija.
lithuania.context: 2021 m. Lietuva leido Vilniuje atidaryti Taivaniečių atstovybę, o Kinija atsakė pažemindama diplomatinius santykius iki laikinųjų reikalų patikėtinių lygio ir taikydama prekybos apribojimus. Nuo 2025 m. gegužės Lietuvoje neliko nė vieno Kinijos diplomato. 2024 m. valdžią perėmę socialdemokratai siekia santykius atkurti, lapkritį Vilniuje lankėsi Kinijos derybininkai.

lithuania.headline: EŽTT: migrantų grąžinimas į Baltarusiją savaime nėra kankinimas
lithuania.summary: EŽTT Didžioji kolegija 11 balsų prieš 6 nusprendė, kad Lietuva nepažeidė kankinimo draudimo, 2022 m. kovą–balandį grąžinusi keturis prieglobsčio prašiusius migrantus į Baltarusiją; išsiuntimas į migraciją kaip ginklą naudojančią šalį savaime nėra pažeidimas, tačiau pažeidžiami asmenys turi būti įvertinti atskirai.
lithuania.why: Apie tai rašė LRT ir BNS
lithuania.context: 2021 m. vasarą Baltarusija ėmė masiškai leisti migrantus per sieną į Lietuvą, Latviją ir Lenkiją, ir šios šalys pradėjo juos apgręžinėti pasienyje. Migrantai kreipėsi į Strasbūrą; byloje prieš Latviją teismas pažeidimą nustatė, nes išsiųsti buvo ir vaikai.

world.headline: US jury convicts Huawei of stealing trade secrets
world.summary: A Brooklyn jury found Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiring to steal trade secrets, bank fraud and sanctions violations over its Iran business, but acquitted it of racketeering; sentencing is set for September 2027 and Huawei plans to appeal.
world.context: US prosecutors charged Huawei in 2019, after its finance chief Meng Wanzhou was arrested in Canada in late 2018; she was held for three years before a deal let her return to China. The US also blacklisted Huawei in 2019, cutting its access to American technology, and the trial ran for more than two months.

world.headline: China investigates Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
world.summary: China's anti-graft watchdog is investigating Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, 62, a politburo member seen as a near-lock for the top Standing Committee; he is the fourth politburo member probed since 2025, and analysts called it the biggest Chinese political news in years.
world.context: Since taking power in 2012, Xi Jinping has run a sweeping anti-corruption campaign that has also removed potential rivals. Since 2025 it has reached the military's top command and three other politburo members: He Weidong, Zhang Youxia and Ma Xingrui.

world.headline: Kilmar Ábrego García leaves US for Spain
world.summary: Kilmar Ábrego García, the Maryland resident wrongly deported to El Salvador in March 2025, has left the US voluntarily for Spain under a deal with the government to avoid forced removal; his lawyers call it temporary until a new administration.
world.context: A judge had barred his deportation to El Salvador in 2019, but in March 2025 the Trump administration sent him to the Cecot mega-prison in what it called an 'administrative error'. After a Supreme Court order he was brought back in June 2025 to face smuggling charges, which a judge later dismissed as political, while officials kept trying to deport him to African countries.

world.headline: US prepares new tariffs on China, EU and others
world.summary: The US may announce as early as Wednesday new tariffs on at least 14 trading partners, including China, the EU and Japan, with rates depending on earlier deals with Trump, following a 'Section 301' probe into overproduction abroad.
world.context: Trump imposed sweeping 'Liberation Day' tariffs in April 2025, then struck trade deals with many partners. This year the Supreme Court ruled those tariffs illegal, and the administration launched a new investigation in March to rebuild them on another legal basis; a US-China interim trade deal expires on 10 January.

interesting.headline: China flies Pakistan's first astronaut to its space station
interesting.summary: China's Shenzhou-24 carried two Chinese astronauts and Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Tiangong station, making him the first foreigner aboard; he will run biotech and materials science experiments during a stay of several days.
interesting.context: Tiangong is China's own space station, completed in 2022.

interesting.headline: Senegal reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations champions
interesting.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport unanimously restored Senegal's 2025 title, ten months after they beat Morocco 1-0 in extra time in a chaotic final but were stripped of the win for walking off in protest at a penalty; Morocco says it will appeal.
interesting.why: Covered by BBC Sport and Al Jazeera
interesting.context: Senegal's walk-off also led football's rule-makers to allow red cards for players who leave the pitch in protest.

interesting.headline: Tidal to delete 27 million AI-generated songs
interesting.summary: From 9 December Tidal will delete all fully AI-generated tracks, about 27 million songs or 6.3% of its catalogue, after 43% of recent uploads proved to be AI-made; music made with AI help is still allowed.
interesting.why: Covered by Ars Technica and TechCrunch
interesting.context: Tidal is a music streaming service; 96% of the AI tracks it hosts had no plays in the past 90 days.

interesting.headline: Claude and ChatGPT's biology skills wow scientists
interesting.summary: Nature reports that new biology abilities in Claude and ChatGPT are impressing researchers and drawing comparisons with DeepMind's AlphaFold.
interesting.context: AlphaFold is DeepMind's protein-structure AI that won a share of the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: Leaked Russian statistics analysed by the BBC show at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died, with the war causing 65% of deaths among Russians aged 18-24 in 2025; Putin called retaliation 'inevitable' after Ukraine hit Russian oil plants.
ongoing.context: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, after seizing Crimea in 2014. Ukraine pushed Russian troops back from Kyiv and later retook Kharkiv and Kherson regions, but the front has since become a grinding war of attrition. Repeated US-led efforts at peace talks have not produced a deal.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: At his first all-hands since returning, Jensen Huang apologised to staff, said he is in therapy and called claims Trump got him rehired 'completely untrue'; Nvidia shares fell 7% as the attorney general dodged questions, and Huang testifies to Congress on 1 December.
ongoing.context: Nvidia's founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 12 November after reports of affairs, including with an executive allegedly linked to Chinese intelligence. On 23 November the board reinstated him, with the White House saying Trump was 'totally involved', and the US blacklisted chip firm Megaspeed.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: Yemen's Houthis struck at Riyadh's tallest tower for a second time and threatened Jeddah and other Red Sea ports, while the Saudi-led coalition hit Hodeidah port.
ongoing.context: Yemen's civil war began in 2014 when the Iran-backed Houthis seized the capital Sanaa. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015, and after years of fighting a truce held from 2022. Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia has flared again alongside the wider war with Iran.
